q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis

**(a) Time left until resolution:**
The earnings release is scheduled for August 26, 2026. Today is August 23, 2026. That leaves approximately 3 days until the forward guidance is announced.

**(b) Most likely outcome and why:**

The question asks for NVIDIA's **forward guidance** (not actual results) for Q2 FY2027 revenue in its earnings release on August 26, 2026.

According to the research provided, NVIDIA has already issued guidance for Q2 FY2027: **$91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%**, which implies a range of approximately $89.2 billion to $92.8 billion.

This guidance was announced during the Q1 FY2027 earnings report (May 20, 2026). When companies issue earnings guidance, they typically maintain that guidance through the quarter unless there are significant changes warranting an update.

With only 3 days remaining until the August 26 earnings release, NVIDIA would only revise guidance if:
- There was a material, unexpected change in demand or business conditions
- They discovered a significant error in their prior guidance
- External circumstances (like new regulations or major customer developments) dramatically altered their outlook

These scenarios are relatively rare in the 2-3 months between initial guidance and earnings release, especially for a company as predictable and stable in execution as NVIDIA has been.

**Most likely scenario:** NVIDIA reiterates its $91.0 billion guidance (or very close to it), within the stated $89.2B-$92.8B range.

**(c) What would push the value lower?**
- Unexpected weakness in data center demand (primary revenue driver)
- Loss of a major customer or significant order cancellation
- Geopolitical developments restricting China sales beyond current assumptions
- Market demand unexpectedly shifts to competitors (AMD, custom chips)
- Manufacturing disruptions or supply chain issues
- Macro recession fears causing customers to delay purchases

**(d) What would push the value higher?**
- Stronger-than-expected demand from AI/data center customers
- Accelerated adoption of newer architectures (e.g., Blackwell ahead of schedule)
- Better execution than originally modeled for existing orders
- New major customer wins or upsell to existing customers
- Revenue recognition timing pulling forward revenue from later quarters
- Upside from business segments outside data center (gaming, automotive, etc.)

**(e) Base rate or historical reference values:**

From the research provided:
- Q1 FY2027 actual revenue: $81.6 billion (reported May 20, 2026)
- Q2 FY2027 guidance: $91.0 billion ± 2% (announced May 20, 2026)
- Wall Street consensus: ~$91.9 billion
- The guidance range: $89.2B to $92.8B

NVIDIA typically provides guidance it can hit or beat. Companies are generally conservative with guidance to avoid missing. The fact that Wall Street's $91.9B average exceeds NVIDIA's $91.0B midpoint suggests the Street believes there's upside potential, but NVIDIA is being prudent.

Historical pattern: Large-cap semiconductor companies like NVIDIA rarely miss their own guidance significantly when it's issued 3 months in advance. The ±2% band is intentionally constructed to give them flexibility.

---

## Reasoning on the forecast range:

The question asks about the **guidance number** that will be announced on August 26, 2026 — not what actual Q2 results will be when they're reported later.

Given:
- Existing guidance of $91.0B ± 2% already in the market
- Only 3 days until the announcement
- No major disclosed developments suggesting a need to revise
- NVIDIA's track record of executing to guidance
- The range provided in the question (99.5B to 115.5B) extends well beyond current guidance

The most probable outcome is that NVIDIA **reiterates** guidance at or very near $91.0 billion, or perhaps slightly adjusts it within the existing $89.2B-$92.8B range.

The probability distribution should be heavily concentrated around $91.0B, with the tail risk scenarios (major upside or downside) less likely given the short timeframe and lack of disclosed material changes.

For the 10th, 50th, and 90th percentiles:
- **10th percentile (downside):** ~$89.5B (modestly conservative revision)
- **50th percentile (median):** ~$91.0B (reiteration of existing guidance)
- **90th percentile (upside):** ~$92.5B (modest upward revision given analyst consensus slightly above)

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA is set to release its Q2 FY2027 earnings on August 26, 2026 [morningstar.com](https://www.morningstar.com/stocks/going-into-earnings-is-nvidia-stock-buy-sell-or-fairly-valued-8). For Q1 FY2027, reported on May 20, 2026, NVIDIA announced record revenue of $81.6 billion, an 85% increase year-over-year [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/).

NVIDIA's guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue is $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). This implies a range from approximately $89.2 billion to $92.8 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). Wall Street analysts' average estimate is approximately $91.9 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), which falls within NVIDIA's guidance range. This outlook does not assume any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). Gross margins are expected to be around 75% [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).
